plan:
## Pitch

**Precision machinist:** Data first. Seventy-two samples, five minutes apart, for `checkout-api` in eu-west-1. A deploy at 14:20. p99 climbs from 180 ms to 640 ms and sits there for twenty minutes. Then I set type. My direction is the **Spike Lathe**. The chart cursor snaps to measured points only. A pinned pair produces a delta readout: "+412 ms p99, 14:15 → 14:35". Set: range selector, cursor chart, pin pair, delta strip.

**Air traffic controller:** One card. One chart. One readout. I start at 360 px and work outward. My direction is the **Tower Strip**: a range selector, a chart with a point readout, and a load status line. Three parts. Anything else has to prove it changes what an on-call engineer does next.

**Furniture designer:** The material is the time series. I defend it. My direction is the **Joinery Card**. Every control returns you to where you were. If you cancel a range switch, the old data stays on screen, not a blank frame. Percentile tiles yield space through a spring that runs at the same speed at 60 Hz and 144 Hz. Set: range selector with cancel, percentile tiles, chart, an undo for the last range change.

**Asteroid workshop tutor:** Teach it through the first useful result. On load, the cursor lands on the worst spike and reads it aloud: "p99 640 ms at 14:35, above the 300 ms SLO." Then the visitor learns to step between spikes. My direction is the **Dock Lesson**. Set: load stages with names, spike stepper, cursor chart, pin. The feeling it should leave behind is "I found it", not "I was lost in a graph".

## Clash

**Precision machinist:** The source bento springs its grid tracks. With 72 real samples on screen, a tile resize that moves the chart is an effect with no useful result. The spring has to earn its frames.

**Air traffic controller:** Checked at 360 px. Four tiles and a chart do not fit side by side. Below 480 px the tiles become one row of chips with no expansion. The spring runs only where there is room.

**Furniture designer:** Where it runs, it uses `k = 1 - (1 - 0.14)^dt` with dt capped at 50 ms. It stops when settled. That part of the source is sound. The idle cycling and hover-to-select are not. Those go.

**Asteroid workshop tutor:** Then the tiles stay, because they teach which line you are reading. Pick p95 and the chart redraws in p95. That is a first useful result in one press.

**Air traffic controller:** The undo for range changes duplicates cancel. Cut it. A cancelled load keeps the previous data, so there is nothing to undo.

**Furniture designer:** Agreed, if cancel restores the previous selection in the range control too. Otherwise the radio says 24h while the chart shows 6h.

**Precision machinist:** Delta strip stays. But it lives inside the pin button's result, not as a seventh part. Two pins give one delta. A third pin replaces the oldest.

**Asteroid workshop tutor:** The weakest state is a failed load. One more pass on that state. Name the stage that failed, keep the old chart, and give one retry button that cannot fire twice.

## Decision

The team builds a single latency card for `checkout-api` where a visitor picks a range, watches named load stages, chooses a percentile, reads any point, steps between SLO breaches, and pins two points to get a delta.

Concept: **Breach Reader**

The machinist set the sample data first. That data gives 72 points, a deploy at 14:20, a 300 ms p99 SLO and four breaches. Every label width was sized from it. The machinist also folded the delta into the pin action. The controller held the 360 px check and cut the undo control. The controller also stopped the tile spring below 480 px. The furniture designer kept the dt-scaled spring and made cancel restore both the data and the range control. The tutor set the opening state with the cursor on the worst breach. The tutor also forced a final pass on the failed-load state.

Rejected direction: the **Tower Strip** at three parts. It reads latency well. It gives no way to find breaches or compare two moments, and those are the two tasks an on-call engineer does after opening the card.

Source: https://github.com/isas1/creative-sites-vault/blob/1595af38a69fbb67c674ef4b90b776a2245c270b/00-components/cards/c16-magnetic-bento.html. The retained mechanism is the rAF loop that eases CSS `fr` track variables toward targets. The step is frame-rate independent, and the loop stops once settled. It appears in row 3 only. Three improvements:
1. Idle demo cycling, hover selection and the `pointerleave` reset are removed. Selection changes only on click, tap, Enter or Space. Tiles are native buttons in a group with `aria-pressed`.
2. `white-space: nowrap` is removed from the detail text. Detail stays visible at reduced weight on inactive tiles. Below 480 px the grid collapses to a chip row with no track animation.
3. The lime palette and 800-weight stats are replaced by the shared tokens. Reduced motion sets tracks directly. The loop does not start while the page is hidden.

The constraint holds in four places. Pressing the active range does nothing. A new range aborts the in-flight load through a generation token, so at most one load exists. The retry button disables while pending. Pinning an already pinned point does nothing.

Six components earn their place. Each answers a separate question in reading latency: which window, is the data ready, which percentile, what value at this moment, where the breaches are, and how two moments compare. Removing any one leaves a question unanswered or pushes it into another control.

## Build notes

1. Ship the sample generator first as `samples.js`. It produces 72 points with a 14:20 deploy and four p99 runs above 300 ms. Size every label width from the longest output before any CSS. The readout width comes from `14:35 · p99 640 ms · +340 over SLO`.
2. Use one `job` object across rows 1 and 2: `{gen, stage, controller}`. `startLoad(range)` returns early when `range === loadedRange && !job`. It aborts any running controller before incrementing `gen`. Retry calls the same function with the button disabled until the job settles.
3. In row 3, guard the rAF loop with `container.clientWidth >= 480 && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches`. Otherwise set the four `--track-*` properties directly. Test at 360 px and 1280 px in both themes before sign-off. This spec makes no claim that those checks were done.

states: idle: hidden status, reached when no load is running
fetching: 'Fetching 24h', reached by range change
aggregating: 'Aggregating 864 samples', reached after fetch resolves
drawing: 'Drawing p99', reached after aggregate
complete: summary line with timestamp, reached after draw
cancelled: 'Cancelled · kept 6h', reached by Cancel
failed: 'Aggregate failed · kept 6h' with Retry, reached by demo failure toggle
reduced-motion: stage ticks without transition

components.name: Percentile tiles
components.description: Four tiles for p50, p95, p99 and error rate. The selected tile expands while neighbours yield track space.
components.purpose: Pick which series the chart plots and show current values for all four.
components.use: Engineer switches from p99 to p50 to check whether the median moved too.
components.input: Click or tap a tile. Keyboard: Tab to a tile, Enter or Space selects.
components.outcome: Selected tile expands to show its detail. The chart redraws in that series.
components.recovery: Selecting another tile reverses the change. Nothing is lost.
components.mechanism: rAF loop eases CSS fr track variables with k = 1 - (1 - 0.14)^dt, dt capped at 50 ms. The loop stops when the summed error drops below 0.002. Below 480 px container width, tiles become a chip row with no track animation.
components.nearestAnalogue: None in recent dates. Source c16 magnetic bento is the direct ancestor.
components.usefulness: Percentile choice changes what a spike means. Current values for all four stay visible.
components.creativeDifference: Track yielding ties layout to selection, while values stay readable during resize.
states: default: p99 selected, reached on load
selected: expanded track with detail and accent border, reached by click or Enter
focus: outline ring, reached by Tab
settled: loop stopped, reached about 400 ms after selection
compact: chip row under 480 px container width
reduced-motion: tracks set directly

components.name: Cursor chart
components.description: SVG line chart with an SLO line and a cursor that snaps to measured samples and reveals the value at that point.
components.purpose: Reveal request latency at a chosen point.
components.use: Engineer drags across the deploy and reads '14:35 · p99 640 ms · +340 over SLO'.
components.input: Pointer move or touch drag over the plot. Keyboard: focus the plot, Left and Right step one sample, Page Up and Page Down step 12, Home and End jump to the ends.
components.outcome: Readout above the plot shows time, value and offset from SLO. Cursor snaps to the nearest real sample.
components.recovery: Escape returns the cursor to the worst breach. Leaving the plot keeps the last cursor position.
components.mechanism: Nearest-index lookup from x position against sample timestamps. Readout has fixed width from the longest sample label. Plot is a focusable element with role group and an aria-live readout.
components.nearestAnalogue: None in recent dates. 2026-10-19 scroll progress maps position to value in one dimension, with no data points.
components.usefulness: This component answers the core need. Snapping prevents reading interpolated values that were never measured.
components.creativeDifference: The readout states distance from SLO, which reframes the number as a decision.
states: initial: cursor on worst breach, reached on load
tracking: cursor follows pointer, reached by pointer or touch
focus: plot outline and key hint, reached by Tab
breach: readout marked over SLO, reached when value exceeds 300 ms
stale: dimmed plot while a new range loads
empty: 'No samples in range', reached when a range returns zero points

components.name: Breach stepper
components.description: Previous and next controls that move the chart cursor between SLO breaches, with a count.
components.purpose: Move directly between moments where latency crossed the SLO.
components.use: Engineer steps 'Breach 2 of 4' to 'Breach 3 of 4' to see whether the second spike followed a deploy.
components.input: Click or tap Previous or Next. Keyboard: Tab to the buttons, Enter or Space. Held keys move one step per keydown.
components.outcome: Cursor jumps to the peak sample of the next breach. Count updates.
components.recovery: The buttons disable at the ends, and the count reads 'Breach 4 of 4'. Escape in the chart returns to the worst breach.
components.mechanism: Breaches are contiguous runs above SLO, computed once per load. Each run is stored by its peak index. A step sets the cursor index directly and replaces any running transition.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-25 breadcrumb in footprints moves through a path. This moves through computed events in data.
components.usefulness: Finding breaches by dragging across 288 points is slow on a phone.
components.creativeDifference: Navigation targets come from the data itself, not from pages or sections.
states: default: 'Breach 1 of 4', reached on load
middle: both buttons enabled
start or end: one button disabled with count at bound
none: 'No breaches in 1h' with both disabled, reached when range has none
focus: visible ring

components.name: Pin pair
components.description: Button that pins the cursor point. Two pins produce a delta line.
components.purpose: Keep two moments and compare them.
components.use: Engineer pins 14:15 and 14:35 and reads '+412 ms p99 over 20 min'.
components.input: Click or tap Pin. Keyboard: Tab to Pin, Enter or Space. P while the chart has focus. Each pin chip has a remove button.
components.outcome: First pin shows a marker. Second pin shows the delta line. A third pin replaces the oldest.
components.recovery: Remove any pin with its x button or Delete on the focused chip. Pinning an already pinned point does nothing.
components.mechanism: A two-slot array keyed by sample index. The label swaps in a reserved width: Pin, Pinned, Replace oldest.
components.nearestAnalogue: 2026-10-20 undo in rewind deals with reversal of an action. This keeps two references and computes between them.
components.usefulness: Before and after a deploy is the comparison on-call engineers report.
components.creativeDifference: The delta is the action's result, so no separate compare panel is needed.
states: empty: 'Pin this point'
one pinned: marker on chart, label 'Pin second point'
pair: delta line shown
full: label 'Replace oldest'
duplicate: label 'Already pinned', no change
cleared: pins removed on range change, with status note

demo.sharedState: One store holds service checkout-api, range (default 6h), load job (generation, stage, status), series (default p99), samples (72 at 5 min), breaches (4 runs above 300 ms), cursorIndex (worst breach), and pins (max 2). The range selector starts a job. Load stages report it and on completion write samples and breaches. The tiles set the series. The chart reads series and samples and writes cursorIndex. The stepper writes cursorIndex from breaches. Pin reads cursorIndex and writes pins. Each file also runs alone with its own copy of the sample data.
